gen_risks.description: Labor market information system and Employability Portal may not become operational as planned.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish detailed implementation plan with milestones, assign dedicated IT lead, pilot test before full rollout, monitor weekly.
gen_risks.evidence: Employment Observatory never fully operationalized, and a digital 'Employability Portal' never launched.

gen_risks.description: Delay in construction of the new multi‑use technical training centre on Príncipe.
gen_risks.mitigation: Finalize design early, adopt fast‑track procurement, include penalty clauses for contractor delays, maintain contingency budget.
gen_risks.evidence: Cost estimate will be refined during implementation following detailed designs, engineering studies, and bidding documents.

gen_risks.description: Procurement delays for equipment and rehabilitation works could postpone activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop detailed procurement schedule, use pre‑qualified vendors, apply accelerated procedures where possible.
gen_risks.evidence: All procurement will be centralized through AFAP and subsequently allocated to recipient institutions.

gen_risks.description: Delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint experienced accountant, customise accounting software for the project, conduct monthly internal audits.
gen_risks.evidence: Delays in recording financial transactions and generating financial reports.

gen_risks.description: Cash‑flow shortfall if the six‑month advance to the designated account is delayed.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain cash reserve, submit quarterly IFRs promptly, negotiate flexible drawdown schedule with the World Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: An advance covering six months’ forecast will be made to the DA following project effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related events may cause short delays in training delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Incorporate climate‑resilient scheduling, secure backup generators, develop contingency plans for training relocation.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate events may cause short delays in implementation of activities in certain areas, such as trainings.

gen_risks.description: Late hiring of required specialists (environmental, social, TVET, data/IT) within 45‑60 days.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare shortlist of qualified candidates before effectiveness, monitor hiring deadlines, report non‑compliance to the Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: Recipient shall cause AFAP to hire … not later than forty‑five (45) days after Effectiveness.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient employer participation in Workforce Development Committees and curriculum design.
gen_risks.mitigation: Offer financial incentives per trainee, formalise WDC terms, hold quarterly stakeholder workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: The project will engage employers in defining priority skills and setting market‑aligned targets.

gen_risks.description: Risk of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment for female participants.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement mandatory GBV/SEA training, establish safe reporting channels, enforce strict code of conduct.
gen_risks.evidence: Risk of sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) and sexual harassment (SH) particularly for young women.

gen_risks.description: Gaps in implementation of GoSTP policies supporting youth employment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set up joint monitoring task‑force with GoSTP, track policy reform milestones, provide technical assistance to close gaps.
gen_risks.evidence: GoSTP has initiated some policies … gaps remain in implementation and coverage.

gen_risks.description: Fragile‑state context may affect project stability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Activate CERC if shocks occur, maintain flexible fund reallocation, engage security advisors.

gen_risks.description: Generation of solid waste and construction debris from rehabilitation works.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require contractors to submit waste‑management plans, conduct site inspections, enforce proper disposal.
gen_risks.evidence: May result in the generation of solid waste, obsolete equipment, and minor construction debris.

gen_risks.description: Exposure to floods, storms, landslides and droughts could damage project facilities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Design facilities to EDGE Level 1 and BRI standards, install flood‑resistant utilities, obtain insurance.
gen_risks.evidence: STP is vulnerable to coastal and riparian floods, severe storms, landslides, and droughts.

gen_risks.description: Training institutions have outdated equipment, limited infrastructure and staffing gaps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Allocate budget for equipment upgrades, provide staff capacity‑building workshops, hire external technical advisors.
gen_risks.evidence: Capacity remains constrained by outdated equipment, limited infrastructure, insufficient operating budgets, staffing gaps.

gen_risks.description: Complex coordination among MLSSS, DTEFP, DPSSF and AFAP may cause delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Draft clear governance charter, schedule regular coordination committee meetings, assign a liaison officer.
gen_risks.evidence: Coordination committee will be established … may recommend adjustments without the need for project restructuring.

gen_risks.description: Changes in destination‑country labour‑market policies could limit labour‑mobility outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Sign MoUs with multiple destination countries, monitor immigration policy changes, develop alternative domestic job pathways.
gen_risks.evidence: Labor mobility approach … depends on partnerships with overseas employers.

gen_risks.description: Fluctuating private‑sector demand in priority value chains may reduce job creation potential.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish labour‑market monitoring unit, adjust curricula annually based on demand data, keep training modules flexible.
gen_risks.evidence: Value‑chain approach … relies on sector demand.

gt_risks.description: Frequent government changes and the cross-ministerial nature of the jobs agenda can shift policy direction, counterpart arrangements, and implementation momentum; further changes may follow the mid-2026 legislative/parliamentary elections. Success depends on sustained coordination across labor, education, tourism, agriculture, and finance ministries plus private-sector engagement.
gt_risks.mitigation: Anchor the project within MLSSS (core employment-promotion mandate); strengthen technical ownership at directorate level rather than relying on political leadership; establish a formal coordination committee and a unified PIU; continue policy dialogue with Government during implementation.

gt_risks.description: STP's fragile growth outlook, narrow fiscal space, and dependence on external financing leave it highly vulnerable to external shocks (energy/food price swings, donor-disbursement delays, climate events), which may weaken labor demand, reduce firms' absorption capacity, and constrain the Government's ability to sustain recurrent-cost interventions (training, stipends, employment services).
gt_risks.mitigation: Prioritize low-cost, scalable interventions; combine supply-side investments with direct job-creation support; target sectors with growth potential and external demand linkages (incl. labor mobility); coordinate with other World Bank macro-fiscal/energy/private-sector engagements in STP.

gt_risks.description: Limited experience of MLSSS and DTEFP in delivering complex labor-market interventions at scale; fragmented institutional landscape; multiple implementation partners; nascent capacity in labor-market analytics, employment intermediation, and cross-sectoral coordination; sustainability risk if new systems/programs are not institutionalized within government structures and budgets.
gt_risks.mitigation: Leverage existing institutions/mechanisms rather than parallel structures (existing MLSSS PIU, coordination committee, AFAP for fiduciary/safeguards); finance targeted TA and staffing; invest in durable institutional assets (labor-market information system, employability portal, strengthened training institutions, formalized service-provider arrangements); use the learning agenda and impact evaluation to identify cost-effective interventions for scale-up.

gt_risks.description: Complex procurement in a small-island context: residual FM risk is moderate but residual procurement risk is substantial, driven by the complexity of civil works in a remote island context, the large number of technical-assistance contracts, and the multiplicity of projects already handled by AFAP.
gt_risks.mitigation: Agree ToRs and technical specifications between AFAP and the World Bank before initiating any procurement (prior and post-review); reinforce AFAP procurement and contract-management capacity incl. specialized support for civil-works supervision; embed dedicated fiduciary controls for the grants/stipends payment mechanism in the Project Operations Manual; continue and adapt the risk assessment during implementation.
